title: Two conditions with SUMIFS
summary: Total sales that match two conditions at once, such as one region and one category, with SUMIFS.

blocks.text: The Nairobi area manager does not only want Nairobi sales. She wants Nairobi sneaker sales, to see whether a new range is working. That is two conditions at the same time: region and category.
SUMIFS adds the numbers on rows where every condition is true. It is SUMIF with room for more conditions.

items: Objective: total a column using two conditions with SUMIFS.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: First say what to add (sum_range), then give each condition as a pair: where to look, then what to match. Add more pairs for more conditions. All ranges must be the same size. A row is added only when all conditions are true.

blocks.caption: Sales list in A1:C8 (sales in K)

blocks.text: Add column C where the region is Mombasa and the category is Sandals. Rows 4 and 8 match: 70 + 55 = 125K.

items: Order matters: SUMIFS starts with the range to add. In SUMIF the range to add comes last, so do not mix them up.
The conditions are joined with AND. A row that is Mombasa but not Sandals is left out.
If no row meets both conditions, the answer is 0, not an error.
Criteria can be typed in quotes or taken from cells, and you can use ">=100" style criteria too. Use $ signs when copying down.

blocks.text: Use the sales list from Training (A1:C8). Type whole numbers, for example 125.

items: SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, criteria_range2, criteria2) adds rows where all conditions are true.
The range to add comes first, unlike SUMIF.
No row meeting all conditions gives 0.
Use cell references for the criteria and $ on the ranges to copy one formula down a summary.

blocks.text: You can now cut sales by any two attributes at once, such as region and category.

items.prompt: In SUMIFS, which range comes first?
How does =SUMIFS(C2:C8,A2:A8,"Nairobi",B2:B8,"Sandals") treat the two conditions?

options.label: It adds rows that are Nairobi and also Sandals
It adds rows that are Nairobi or Sandals
It uses only the first condition
It returns an error, because SUMIFS takes one condition
